text:
Accuracy is used to hit a target with an attack, and is checked against the target's Evasion to determine that chance. Accuracy is also used to check against Deflection chance.
Player characters inherently gain 6 base accuracy per level, and 6 base accuracy for each point of dexterity.

title: Acolyte of Chayula
text:
The Acolyte of Chayula has uncovered the secrets of the Dreamer and embraced the madness which entail it. With Embrace the Darkness, he can give up his Spirit in exchange for Darkness that absorbs damage. Waking Dream spawns Flames of Chayula remnants that can be picked up to gain recovery or chaos damage, which Lucid Dreaming will cause all Flames to spawn as one type. The Acolyte has a number of passives that grant or enhance chaos damage, such as Sap of Nightmares to gain chaos damage leech, Inner Turmoil to build up and maintain Volatility more easily, and Unravelling to cause chaos damage to inflict an elemental ailment. In addition, he can learn Void Illusion that leave behind explosive illusions on dodge roll, and Chayula's Gift to build up chaos resistance.
Upon meeting with the Dreamer himself, he will bestow upon his Acolyte a special gift: the ability to briefly transform into an Archon of Chayula to unleash chaotic devastation.

title: Acrobatics
text: Acrobatics is a keystone passive skill that allows all types of hits to be evaded, at the cost of greatly reducing the user's evasion rating.

title: Acrobatics
text: This keystone allows players to evade area of effect skills as well as strike or projectile skills. The 75% less Evasion Rating modifier applies multiplicative with other sources of evasion reduction, such as ...and Protect me from Harm.

title: Ailment
text:
Ailments are a type of debuff associated with specific damage types. Damaging ailments damage over time.
Damaging ailments: bleeding, poison, and ignite.
Non-damaging ailments: chill, freeze, shock and electrocute.

title: Ailment
text:
The chance for most ailments to be applied generally depends on the amount of damage dealt before mitigation compared to the defender's ailment threshold value. A player's base ailment threshold is based on half of their maximum life. This scaling is different for monsters; monster ailment threshold scales with monster level and is independent of monster life. Immobilization effects, such as freeze, electrocute, pin and stun use a different value called "poise". Both of these values have their own multiplier depending on rarity of the monster .
Chill will always be applied as long as the damage meets the minimum ailment threshold to not be discarded, though its slow magnitude scales with the ailment threshold formula.
The chance to inflict poison or bleeding is based on a static numerical chance instead rather than being calculated via the ailment threshold formula.
The chance to inflict an ailment is multiplicative against the chance to avoid an ailment. If the defender has 100% chance to avoid an ailment, they cannot be inflicted with that ailment, even by constant ground effects that usually bypass ailment avoidance chance.

title: Ailment
text:
Player ailment threshold is based on half of their maximum life by default, though modifiers can cause it to also scale from other stats such as Energy Shield or Mana instead.
Monster Ailment and Poise Thresholds depend on monster level. The values can be found in the table below. Unlike in Path of Exile 1, these thresholds are independent of monster life.

title: Ailment
text: Some effects may cause an ailment to spread to other nearby targets. Spreading an ailment inflicts a new, matching ailment on another target, from the same source. The new ailment can potentially spread further, but never back to the same target twice.

text:
This only includes ailments which directly deal damage themselves, not those which amplify damage from other sources. Some support gems or passives may use this term to collectively refer to all of these ailments.
Bleeding

title: Amazon
text: The Amazon is an elite warrior trained to protect the Azmeri elders, transforming her into an offensive powerhouse with recovery and Evasion bonuses to boot. She can learn Elemental Infusion to use charges to infuse her attacks with lightning damage explosions (or elemental damage explosions with Surging Avatar), Critical Strike and Penetrate to turn Accuracy into a source of damage, and Predatory Instinct to deal more damage against enemies at certain life intervals. Azmeri Brew lets her flasks pull double duty on life and mana recovery, and Mystic Harvest grants her elemental life leech. Finally, Stalking Panther grants her more Evasion from her gear except the body armour.

title: Archmage
text: Archmage is a Spirit gem which causes your non-Channelling spells to cost additional mana and deal extra Lightning damage, both based on your maximum Mana.

title: Area of effect
text: Area of Effect, (AoE for short), refers to skills that strike an area rather than a specific target. This area could range form a line to a cone to circle.

title: Area of effect
text:
This skill has an effect that applies to every target in its area, rather than picking specific targets. Areas of Effect that originate from a target hit by a Skill will add that target's size to their radius.
Dodge roll does not grant avoidance towards AoE attacks.

title: Armour
text: Armour is a defence that provides damage reduction to incoming physical damage from hits. The % of damage reduced depends on the size of the incoming hit relative to the armour value and cannot exceed 90%. Armour is associated with strength.

title: Armour
text:
Armour grants physical damage reduction, with the exact amount of damage reduction depending on the ratio of armour to the physical damage of the hit. If the armour value is significantly larger than the damage, most of the damage is prevented. If the armour value is similar to or less than the incoming damage, only a small percentage of that damage will be prevented. As a result, armour is more effective against many smaller hits rather than fewer larger hits, even if the total damage dealt would be identical.
Armour never mitigates damage over time, as armour only applies to hits. Bleed is an ailment that deals physical damage over time that is based on the physical damage dealt by a skill before mitigation; armour will reduce the hit damage but not the damage over time. However, both the hit damage and the damage over time can be mitigated with sources of #% additional Physical Damage Reduction. The maximum total physical damage reduction from all sources is 90%.

title: Armour
text:
To prevent one third of damage (33%), you need armour 5 times the damage (e.g. 500 armour for 100 damage)
To prevent half of damage (50%), you need armour 10 times the damage (e.g. 1000 armour for 100 damage)
To prevent two thirds of damage (66%), you need armour 20 times the damage (e.g. 2000 armour for 100 damage)
To prevent three quarters of damage (75%), you need armour 30 times the damage (e.g. 3000 armour for 100 damage)
To prevent 90% of damage, you need armour 90 times the damage (e.g. 9000 armour for 100 damage)
When the damage of a hit significantly exceeds Armour, it will never prevent more damage than the armour value divided by 10 (e.g. 1000 armour will never prevent more than 100 damage at its minimum percentage prevention).

title: Armour
text: Armour Break is a debuff that reduced Armour by a specified amount. When a target's Armour is broken to 0, it has Fully Broken Armour, which interact with certain mechanics. Enemies (but not players) with Fully Broken Armour also take 20% increased physical damage from hits.

title: Armour Break
text: Armour Break is a debuff that reduces armour by a specified amount. When the target's armour is reduced to 0 by this effect, they will have Fully Broken Armour, which interacts with certain effects.

title: Armour Break
text:
Armour Break lasts for 12 seconds, after which the debuff is removed. If the target's armour value reaches 0 from this, the debuff is replaced with "Fully Broken Armour" which lasts 12 seconds (4 seconds on players). Reapplying Armour Break on a target will refresh the duration of the debuff, but any further Armour Break will not be applied while the target has Fully Broken Armour.
Fully Broken Armour also causes the affected target to take 20% increased physical damage from hits. This does not affect player characters.
The amount of armour broken is tripled against Normal monsters and doubled against Magic monsters.
The Warbringer passive Imploding Impacts allows Armour to be broken below 0. The maximum amount of negative armour a target can have is the inverse of its original armour value; for example, an enemy with 1000 armour can be broken up to -1000 Armour. Negative armour grants a damage multiplier rather than a damage reduction at the same ratio. Mechanics that interact with Fully Broken Armour will function the same way against targets with negative armour.

title: Ascendancy class
text: Ascendancy classes, or simply "ascendancies," are subclasses that allow players to further refine their character's class by making use of special abilities, skills, and modifiers that enable certain archetypes. Ascendancies can be unlocked by completing Ascension Trials through the campaign and endgame. For more information on each trial and their requirements, see the Ascension Trials page.

title: Ascendancy class
text:
Currently, there are 22 regular ascendancy classes available. All classes are planned to have access to 3 ascendancy classes (not counting alternate ones), for a total of 36.
Choosing an ascendancy class after completing an Ascension Trial for the first time will unlock a unique ascendancy skill tree that functions similarly to the larger Passive Skill Tree: the player earns ascendancy skill points which can be spent on allocating nodes granting passive bonuses and in some cases special skills. The tree can be accessed anytime from the center of the Passive Skill Tree window. Players can complete 4 tiers of Ascension Trials, each granting 2 ascendancy skill points for a total of 8.
Some ascendancy classes have hidden passives that are unlocked by fulfilling certain conditions, such as by allocating specific ascendancy passives or by progressing endgame encounter quests.

title: Ascendancy class
text: Alternate versions of existing ascendancy classes can also be unlocked. Currently, the Abyssal Lich is the only alternate ascendancy available and is unlocked by defeating Vessel of Kulemak at full power while the player has already ascended into a Lich.

title: Attack
text:
Attacks are skills that directly use your equipped weapon to damage enemies. Spells are not attacks.
The base damage, attack speed and critical hit chance of an attack are determined using your weapon's stats unless a skill says otherwise.
Attacks do not necessarily deal physical damage, they can deal any damage type.

title: Attribute
text:
Strength, dexterity, and intelligence are attributes. Attributes are often requirements of gems and equipment. Characters gain inherent bonuses from attributes.
Attributes can be obtained either through items or through the passive skill tree.

title: Attribute
text:
Strength is required to equip most equipment that grants Armour, as well as various melee-aligned Weapons and Skills. Every 1 Strength grants +2 Life.
Dexterity, is required to use most equipment that grants Evasion Rating, as well as various range-aligned Weapons and Skills. Every 1 Dexterity grants +6 Accuracy Rating.
Intelligence is required to use most equipment that grants Energy Shield, as well as various spell-aligned Weapons and Skills. Every 1 Intelligence grants +2 Mana.

title: Bleeding
text:
Bleeding deals 75% of a hit's physical damage dealt (before mitigation and damage taken modifiers) as physical damage over time over 5 seconds. Bleeding on monsters (not players) deal an extra 100% damage while the target is moving, or if the bleeding is Aggravated. This percentage is affected multiplicatively by ailment magnitude. Ailment damage cannot be scaled directly; however, it can be indirectly scaled by modifying the hit damage.
Bleeding does not stack; each instance of bleeding has an independent duration and only the highest damage instance of bleeding will deal damage.
Bleeding chance depends on an explicit chance to inflict Bleeding.
The damage over time from bleeding bypasses energy shield and damages life directly. It also cannot be redirected to another resource, such as to Mana with Mind Over Matter.
Note that bleeding can be applied by any skill that can hit, not exclusively attacks.

title: Bleeding
text:
Aggravate is a mechanic primarily related to bleeding. When a bleeding debuff is aggravated, it causes that bleeding debuff to permanently deal extra base damage over time, equivalent to if the target was moving. This multiplier does not stack even if the target is actually moving.
Each instance of aggravated bleeding is independent from all other instances of bleeding. A bleeding debuff that is aggravated will remain aggravated until its duration expires.

title: Bleeding
text: Blood Loss refers to the total amount of damage a target has taken from physical damage over time, which includes Bleeding. Blood Loss amount is shown as a darker red bar on the target's life bar and is used for certain skills.

title: Bleeding
text: Incision is a stacking debuff that applies +10% chance to apply Bleeding per stack. When a target becomes inflicted with Bleeding, all stacks of Incision are removed from them.

title: Block
text: Block is a type of damage mitigation that negates damage coming incoming hits. Passive chance to block can be obtained primarily from shields. Certain skills allow active methods of blocking, limited by the player's stun threshold.

title: Block
text:
When a hit is blocked, all incoming damage from that hit is prevented, unless you have a modifier that causes some damage from blocked hits to be bypassed. Blocking only works against hits (including self-hitting) and does nothing against damage over time or life loss. The character can still receive debuffs such as Stun and Freeze coming from the blocked hit despite the damage being negated.

title: Block
text: Certain monsters (usually bosses) can use attacks which cannot be blocked, which will be indicated by the enemy flashing red when used. Damage over time and other damage that does not come from a hit cannot be blocked.

title: Blood Mage
text: The Blood Mage puts her Life on the line in exchange for power. The Blood Mage must take Sanguimancy as her first skill, causing skills to have a life cost on top of mana cost, but also causing killed monsters to drop Life Remnants that recover life which can Overflow. From there on, she gains access to passives that grant powerful bonuses to Critical Hits and life-based defenses and recovery, the ability to have elemental damage to scale Bleeding, curses that reserve enemy life and prevent life regeneration, and turning life flask charges into a source of damage.

title: Blood Magic
text: These unique items have the Blood Magic modifier, which grants the effects of this keystone. These effects do not double up by also having the keystone allocated.

title: Chaos
text:
Chaos damage is one of the five damage types. It can be mitigated by chaos resistance. Chaos damage has the effect of removing twice as much energy shield when dealing damage.
Chaos damage over time is usually inflicted by poison or other debuffs.

title: Chaos
text:
Chaos damage is somewhat rarer than the other damage types, and is more often seen as damage over time rather than hit damage. It is stronger against energy shield, but a character with Chaos Inoculation is completely immune to chaos damage.
Chaos damage is usually used alongside Withered, a stacking debuff that increases chaos damage taken.

title: Chaos Inoculation
text:
CI grants immunity to chaos damage, therefore causing the player to be unaffected by poison or other chaos damage over time effects. It also grants immunity to bleeding. It does not prevent Corrupted Blood or other physical damage over time sources.
The player's stun and ailment thresholds will be based on the new value of 1 maximum life, instead of being based on the amount of maximum life you would have without this keystone. It is recommended to take passives that grant additional stun and ailment threshold based on your energy shield to counteract them.
While CI is allocated, a player always counts as being on full life but can never be on low life.
Any effects that cause damage to bypass your energy shield (e.g. Heavy Buffer notable) will cause you to die instantly on taking damage if not fully redirected (e.g. Mind over Matter). Additionally, life loss effects will cause death if not countered with an equivalent amount of life regeneration; however, this can still result in death due to effects that disable or reduce life regeneration/recovery.

title: Charm
text: Charm is an item class of trinkets that function somewhat similarly to utility flasks from the first Path of Exile. Charms gain charges from killing monsters or refilling at wells and will trigger automatically to grant defensive bonuses or immunities to negative status effects.

title: Charm
text:
Charms cannot be activated manually. While a charm has sufficient charges, it is used automatically when it meets the conditions specified by its implicit modifier. When used, they will grant its effect for the listed charm duration. It cannot be reused until the duration expires.
If two charms of the same type are equipped, meeting the activation requirements will only activate one charm at a time. Different charm types can activate simultaneously.
Charms gain charges from killing monsters, using the Well, or activating a checkpoint, the same way flasks do. Charms can also roll a modifier that grants a small number of charges each second. Unequipping a charm will remove all charges on the charm.
Charm slots are primarily granted by belts, which grant one to three charm slots when equipped, indicated by its implicit mod. Additional charm slots can also be obtained from certain passive skills and belt explicit mods. Up to 3 charm can be equipped at a time. The quest Ancient Vows grants +1 charm slot as a reward.
The number of charm slots a belt can provide depend on its item level:
Charms can only be normal, magic or unique. There are no rare charms.

title: Charm
text: Quality on charms increases the duration of the charm's effect by the quality percentage. Currently, the only way to obtain a charm with quality is to have it drop randomly with quality or by corrupting it.

title: Chronomancer
text: The Chronomancer can manipulate time, gaining access to a variety of utility skills and other bonuses. She can refresh all cooldowns on command with Time Snap or stop all enemies in their tracks with Time Freeze. She can delay some damage taken with Phased Form and cast Temporal Rift to rewind her position and life, mana, and energy shield values back a few seconds while undoing any delayed damage, and Inevitable Agony applies a powerful damage amplification debuff that takes times to kick in. In addition, Quicksand Hourglass grants a fluctuating bonus to skill speed or area of effect, Now and Again grants a chance for her skills to repeat, and Apex of the Moment grants her a slowing aura.

title: Critical hit
text: A critical hit, or simply crit, is a property of hits that gains a damage multiplier based on its critical damage bonus. Additionally, critical hits can often enable or trigger other effects from items or passive skills.

title: Critical hit
text:
When a skill is used or triggered, it performs a critical hit check by rolling a number. This roll ranges from 0 to 99.99, determining a threshold the skill's critical hit chance must exceed to deal a critical hit successfully.
For example: A player casts a spell and rolls a 12. When enemies are hit, those hits require a critical strike chance of 12.01% or greater to deal a critical hit.
While hits from the same skill will usually have the same critical hit chance, resulting in all-or-nothing behaviour, conditional modifiers and buffs/debuffs can cause critical hit chance to differ between enemies.
Critical hits are rolled for all hits from that skill. If a critical hit chance roll succeeds, all hits from that skill will be a critical hit.
This does not apply to Sustained and Channelling skills which hit continuously while channelling. Sustained skill will roll critical hit chance for each hit individually, and channelling skills will roll critical hit chance for each cast interval of the channelled skill.
Multi-projectile skills from players and allies roll crit independently, but projectiles from a monster's skill will either all crit or not crit.
If critical hit chance is lucky, skills perform two crit checks and keep the lower requirement. If it is unlucky, the higher requirement is kept.

title: Critical hit
text:
If the user has Inevitable Critical Hits from Forced Outcome, failed critical hit chance rolls will be rerolled until it succeeds. Each time crit chance is rerolled, 30% less critical damage bonus will be applied to the final hit. This less critical hit damage penalty is additive; after 4 failed crit rolls, the hit will automatically become a crit.
If critical hit chance is bifurcated, skills perform two crit checks that apply independently. If both are successful, critical hit damage bonus is applied twice. Luck applies to each bifurcated critical hit independently.
If a critical hit can be evaded, such as from an attacks or by a monster, but the evasion check fails and lands a hit, evasion is checked again; if the the evasion check succeeds, the hit is downgraded to a non-critical hit. This does not affect the evasion entropy value.

title: Critical hit
text:
Martial weapons have a base critical hit chance which is used for almost all attack skills. Unarmed skills have a base critical hit chance of 5%.
Skills that use two weapons simultaneously calculate each hand's crit chance and damage separately, which are later combined into a single instance of damage. If either hand crits, the combined hit is considered a single crit. This does not retroactively scale a hand that non-crits, however.
Skills that use two weapons independently calculate crit chance independently for each hit.
Spells instead specify a base critical hit chance on the skill itself which can then be further modified.
Other allies including minions have an independent critical hit chance separate from the player.
Modifiers that grant additional base critical hit chance (e.g. Critical Weakness, Critical Strike) are applied before modifiers that grant increased/decreased/more/less critical hit chance.
Effects which prevent critical strikes (e.g. Resolute Technique) take priority over effects that causes you to always deal critical strikes.

title: Critical hit
text: Critical hits deal extra damage compared to a non-critical hit, the magnitude of which is determined by a stat called critical damage bonus, equivalent to "critical strike multiplier" or "crit multi" from Path of Exile 1. Critical damage bonus is a unique multiplier independent of all other damage multipliers. The default critical damage bonus for players and minions is +100%, or 200% of base damage. Monsters have 40% less bonus critical damage.

title: Curse
text: Curses are Debuffs that apply a certain downside on the recipient, weakening them. By default, the player can apply a maximum of one Curse on an enemy, which can be increased. Curse skills can only apply the curse on enemies within a certain monster level, which increases with gem level.

title: Curse

title: Damage
text:
Damage is the process by which a player or monster's life or energy shield is reduced.
Damage is always one of 5 damage types: physical, chaos, fire, cold or lightning.
Damage can be mitigated or prevented by various defences.
Damage can have various keywords which affect its calculation.
Receiving damage

title: Damage conversion
text: Damage conversion is a conversion mechanic that changes a portion of the damage type of a hit into another damage type. The converted damage is only affected by modifiers to their new damage type, and are not scaled through their original damage type. Damage conversions do not apply to damage over time. In general, conversion is a two step process - inherent conversion from skills gems apply first, then conversion from other sources like support gems, items, and the passive skill tree apply to the remainder; however, there are some additional caveats described below.

title: Damage conversion
text:
Conversion can exist in two forms:
Regular conversion: e.g. #% of [Damage Type] Converted to [Damage Type]
Gain conversion: e.g. Gain #% of [Damage Type] as Extra [Damage Type]
The difference between these forms is the effect they have on the source damage: Regular conversion removes the damage from the source type, while gain conversion leaves it intact. Both occur simultaneously, unless the regular conversion is inherent to a skill.

title: Damage conversion
text:
Damage conversion is calculated after combining any sources of additional damage to base damage, but before any damage modifiers (e.g. increased or more damage). See receiving damage for further information on damage order.
Damage can be converted from any damage type to any other damage type, with no restrictions on order. This differs from Path of Exile 1, which had a strict order of damage conversion.

title: Damage conversion
text: Converted damage does not retain its original damage type; only the final damage type is used for scaling. title: Damage over time
text:
Damage over time refers to damage which happens gradually over a duration instead of all at once.
Damage over time does not count as a hit, so bonuses and defences that affect hit damage will not affect it. Resistance in the appropriate damage type will mitigate damage over time but armour and penetration will not as they only apply to hits.

title: Deadeye
text: The Deadeye is a class focused around ranged offense. She can make her projectile skills more effective by giving them more damage at close or far range and adding an extra projectile. The Deadeye can also gain access to Tailwind, which improves her speed, evasion, and deflection amount as long as she avoids taking damage, or improve her frenzy charge generation and consumption. The Deadeye can also specialize in marks by learning Called Shots to autonomously apply marks on enemies or Bullseye to apply Critical Weakness to marked enemies. She can also summon mirages that fire more projectiles with Mirage Deadeye.

title: Defences
text:
Defences is a term referring collectively to armour, evasion and energy shield. They are primarily gained through the inherent stats of worn equipment. This term is no longer in use as a keyword in game. Other defensive stats such as runic ward, block, and resistances are not considered defences.
These stats are respectively associated with the three attributes, strength, dexterity and intelligence, and equipment (other than jewellery) which grants each defence will also have the associated attribute requirement.

title: Deflection
text: Deflection is type of mitigation. It grants a chance to take less damage from a hit by a percentage. Like Evasion, chance to deflect is based on the defender's Deflection Rating against the attacker's Accuracy Rating. Most sources of Deflection Rating scale with the user's Evasion Rating, acting as a supplementary mitigation tool for evasion-based builds.

title: Dexterity
text: Dexterity (or Dex) is one of three attributes, along with Strength and Intelligence. Dexterity is required to equip most evasion rating-granting armour, as well as ranged and some melee weapons and skills. Characters gain +6 accuracy rating per dexterity.

title: Dexterity
text:
Characters start with a certain amount of base dexterity based on their character class.
Pure dexterity character classes (Ranger and Huntress) start with 15 Dexterity.

The Druid is an Ezomyte who was once part of the Druids of Skothe, an ancient order that venerated the Azmeri Draíocht and practiced the mystic arts of the Maji. The Druids were wiped out by the King in the Mists and his cultists, who deceived them by disguising himself as a Maji of the old.

text: This keystone converts your base energy shield (the sum of sources of flat energy shield) into base mana. This conversion applies before any modifiers, such as #% increased/more Mana. This mana will not scale with modifiers to energy shield (e.g. #% increased/more Energy Shield).

title: Elemental damage
text: Elemental damage collectively refers to the damage type of Fire, Cold or Lightning. Any bonus to elemental damage affects all three of these damage types.

title: Endurance charge
text:
Endurance charges are a resource that players can gain and generate in various ways. Charges do not inherently grant bonuses to the character or monsters; they are used to empower skills by being consumed by them.
Endurance charges, like other charges, have a default duration of 15 seconds and a maximum of 3.

title: Energy Shield
text: Energy Shield (abbreviated as ES) is one of the three core defences that can be found on equipment. It is associated with intelligence and acts as an additional hit points on top of life that recharges over time if the defender does not lose energy shield or life for a short duration. Bleeding and poison damage bypasses energy shield to damage life directly, while chaos damage deals twice as much damage against energy shield.

title: Energy Shield
text:
Energy shield protects life by being depleted first before taking damage to life.
The damage inflicted on Energy Shield is calculated after all damage mitigation factors, such as physical or elemental resistances, have been taken into account.
Damage from Bleeding and Poison bypass energy shield, damaging life directly. Certain items may also cause damage to bypass energy shield.
Chaos damage removes twice as much energy shield as other damage types. This does not affect the overall damage dealt. In the case that Chaos Damage deals damage to both Energy Shield and Life (or Mana) in a single instance of damage, it will not affect the Life or Mana removed.

title: Energy Shield
text:
If energy shield is not at full and life or energy shield have not been lost for a short delay (also known as "start of Energy Shield Recharge"), it will begin to recharge 12.5% of maximum energy shield per second. Energy shield recharge is considered a form of recovery, but it is not regeneration. Any damage taken to Life or ES will interrupt recharge, restarting the delay timer.
Other forms of recovery do not interact with recharge.

title: Evasion
text: Evasion is one of the three core defences that can be found on equipment. It is associated with dexterity and provides an entropy-based system of damage avoidance against most types of hits. Evasion chance is based on your Evasion Rating versus the enemy's Accuracy Rating.

text:
Evading an attack prevents all damage from the attack and other hit-related effects. For projectiles, evasion prevents collision. Chance to evade/chance to hit is determined by a function of the defender's evasion rating against the attacker's accuracy rating. Chance to hit cannot go below 5%; likewise, chance to evade cannot exceed 95%.

text: If a hit makes an evasion check and the check fails, leading to a hit, and that hit would deal a critical hit, the chance to evade is tested again independently. If this check is passed, the critical hit is downgraded to a non-critical hit, or rerolled if the attacker has Forced Outcome.

title: Evasion
text:
Player attacks have an accuracy penalty that drops off with distance from the attacker between 2 metres (no penalty) and 9 metres (90% less accuracy rating); this primarily affects projectile skills.

title: Evasion
text:
Evasion is not a random system. Instead, it uses a deterministic "entropy" system that ensures a hit will occur after a certain number of evades:
If it is the first time an entity is attacked, or if the time since the last attempted hit exceeds 100 server ticks (3.33 seconds), randomize the entropy value from 0-99.
Calculate the attacker's chance to hit against the defender's chance to evade, and add this integer to the entropy value.
If the resulting entropy value is lower than 100, the hit counts as evade. When the value reaches 100 or greater, the check counts as a hit, and subtract 100 from the entropy value.
The secondary critical hit downgrade test does not affect the entropy value.
As a result, if a player has a 1 in N chance to be hit, then the player will be hit exactly once for every N consecutive attacks. This eliminates all possibilities of lucky and/or unlucky streaks. It is still based on chance because of the entropy's value randomization in the first step. Note that if multiple mobs are attacking one character, all of the mobs' attacks share the same entropy value. The chance to evade shown in the character stats window is based on the average accuracy of a monster at the player's level.

text:
When defending against monster hits, there is no distinction between attacks and spells and will apply to any attack from enemies except boss attacks with a red flash.
When attacking monsters, their evasion provides avoidance against all attack hits, interacting with accuracy/chance to hit. Monsters cannot evade spell hits.

title: Flask
text: A flask is a item which are used to recover life and mana. Each use of a flask requires a certain amount of flask charges to be expended. Modifiers on flasks can adjust how it gains or uses its flask charges or add additional effects when used.

title: Flask
text:
There are two types of flasks: life flasks and mana flasks. When used, they will recover life or mana, respectively, over time. A player can have only one life flask and one mana flask equipped at a time unless otherwise specified.
Flask charges are gained by killing monsters, using the Well, or activating a checkpoint. The amount and chance of gaining a flask charge on kill is based on the monster's rarity. There are modifiers which modify the amount of charges gained or used. Some modifiers will cause the flask to gain charges passively over time. Unequipping a flask will remove all charges on the flask.
Flasks can only be normal, magic or unique. There are no rare flasks.

title: Freeze
text: Freeze or frozen is a non-damaging cold ailment that causes targets to be unable to act by fully slowing their action speed and immobilising them. Monsters killed while frozen will shatter, leaving behind no corpse.

title: Freeze
text:
Freeze reduces action speed to 0, preventing movement and usage of skills. The duration of freeze depends on the damage taken by the enemy after mitigation relative to the enemy's ailment threshold.
If a hit that can freeze fails to do so due to not reaching the minimum ailment threshold, it will instead add to a counter called Freeze Buildup. When freeze buildup reaches or exceeds 100%, it will apply a fixed duration freeze to the target, then reset the counter to 0%.
Each time a boss monster is frozen either directly or by accumulating freeze buildup, its ailment threshold against freeze increases. This value decreases over time to its base value.
Blocking a hit does not prevent it from applying freeze buildup.

title: Frenzy charge
text:
Frenzy charges are a resource that players can gain and generate in various ways. Charges do not inherently grant bonuses to the character or monsters; they are used to empower skills by being consumed by them.
Frenzy charges, like other charges, have a default duration of 15 seconds and a maximum of 3.

title: Gem

title: Ghost Dance
text:
The character must be hit to lose a Ghost Shroud and to recover energy shield. Defensive mechanics that prevent a hit from occurring such as evasion also prevents the loss of Ghost Shrouds.
Block also prevents loss of Ghost Shrouds. Taking damage from blocked hits (e.g. through Glancing Blows) does not change this.
Self-hits will cause a Ghost Shroud to be lost normally.
Unlike its Path of Exile counterpart, and contrary to the skill's description and stats (which are identical to POE1), the energy shield recovery does not occur after taking damage.[Likely due to a bug] Currently, the recovery applies inconsistently:
If at full energy shield, a Ghost Shroud will be consumed, but no recovery will occur and the character takes the expected damage from the hit.

title: Ghost Dance
text: If not at full energy shield, a Ghost Shroud is consumed and the recovery occurs immediately before taking damage, but both are considered simultaneous for loss calculations. It is not considered a mitigation/damage reduction effect. This means that even if no energy shield loss is visible or energy shield is higher after the hit (e.g. the recovery exceeds damage taken), it can still result in being inflicted with ailments from the damage taken, but will not cause recharge to be interrupted due to energy shield loss never actually occurring (i.e. going from a higher ES value to a lower ES value).

title: Ignite
text: Ignite is a damaging ailment that deals fire damage over time. Skills that deal fire damage over time deal ignite damage. Fire damage hits have chance to apply ignite based on the magnitude of Flammability on the target.

title: Ignite
text:
Ignite deals 80% of a hit's fire damage dealt (before mitigation and damage taken modifiers) as fire damage over time over 4 seconds. This percentage is affected multiplicatively by ailment effect/magnitude.
Because the damage ignites deal is not modified by player damage, and instead only modified by ignite magnitude and enemy resistances, ignites mostly depend upon the source which created the ignite to determine the ignite's damage output. The damage an ignite deals can still be indirectly modified by increasing the original source of damage which contributed to the ignite.
Ignite does not stack; each instance of ignite has an independent duration and only the highest damage instance of ignite will deal damage.
Ignite does not double-dip on enemy resistance. Ignite is applied before resistance is calculated for the igniting hit, then resistance is applied to both the hit and the ignite separately.

title: Ignite
text:
The chance for hits to apply ignite depends on the total magnitude of all Flammability debuff stacks on the target, which itself is dependent on the amount of pre-mitigation fire damage dealt relative to the monster's ailment threshold. Each 1% Flammability magnitude grants 1% chance to Ignite per 5% of ailment threshold a hit deals, up to 100% Flammability magnitude. This can include other damage types if they can contribute to Ignite magnitude. Each stack of Flammability has an independent additive magnitude.

title: Infernalist
text: The Infernalist calls upon demonic forces to unleash hellish flames and gain great power at a cost. Pyromantic Pact trades Mana for Infernal Flame, where paying mana cost instead fills up a meter which causes her to take fire damage when filled. It can then be enhanced to grant the Elemental Archon buff while Infernal Flame is kept high but not full. Altered Flesh grants damage taken conversion and opens up three contracts with Beidat, reserving a quarter of your life in exchange for more Mana, Energy shield, or Spirit based on maximum Life. She also has access to a loyal Hellhound companion, a powerful boost to critical hits that inflict self-ignite, and the ability to have all damage types inflict Ignite.

title: Infusion
text: Infusions are a stackable buffs which can be consumed by certain spells to gain additional effects. They are generated as remnants that spawn from certain skills.

title: Infusion
text:

text: The Invoker is attuned to nature, providing mastery over the elements. He can empower his elemental attacks with critical hits that ignore resistances and trigger Elemental Expression to wipe out enemies, or unleash Unbound Avatar to gain a massive boost to his elemental offense after applying elemental ailments enough times. title: Iron Reflexes
text:
Iron Reflexes is a keystone passive skill that removes all evasion rating and converts it to armour.
Iron Reflexes essentially converts all sources of flat Evasion Rating to flat Armour, which is then multiplied by your "increased Armour" value as well as any "more Armour" modifiers. "Increased Evasion" and "More Evasion" become effectively useless.

title: Iron Reflexes
text:
The final Armour value is calculated with the following formula:
(Flat AR  + Flat EV) * (1 + [total #% increased/reduced AR]) * (More/Less AR modifiers)
where:
AR = Armour
Flat EV = Sum of Evasion Rating from Equipped Items (e.g. Body Armour, Shield) and other sources of additional (flat) Evasion Rating
Flat AR = Sum of Armour from Equipped Items (e.g. Body Armour, Shield) and other sources of additional (flat) Armour
More/Less modifiers from different sources are multiplicative with each other.

title: Lich
text: The Lich is a class who has become one with death, unlocking the potential to acquire great power at a price. She can apply everlasting curses to her enemies that make them explode on death, grant herself and her minions Unholy Might as long as she can prevent her Mana from running low, or empower her spells by consuming power charges or sacrificing energy shield. title: Life
text:
Life (also named Health or Hit Points) is the main health source of a character or monster and it decreases when receiving damage; when it reaches 0% the entity dies.
For characters it means that it must be resurrected in town or checkpoint, for monsters it means complete death and it can be only revived by other monsters, or by players as a minion.
Players can recover life by using life flask, gaining life regeneration from passive skills and equipment, or leeching life from enemies. Life is also fully restored upon entering a town or hideout.

title: Life
text:
Life starts at 28 for level 1 characters, before factoring additional life from levels or Strength.
Characters gain +12 maximum Life per Player Level, +2 maximum Life per Strength.

title: Life
text:
There are a few different ways to lose life points. Certain mechanics applies or not depending on how life is lost.
Life Loss
Life Loss is not damage, and can't be mitigated or redirected to other resources, such as Energy Shield. Life Loss is immediate and can kill you.
Sacrificed life
Sacrificed Life is Life loss (not damage), but you cannot sacrifice your own Life if it would reduce it below 1 Life. You can sacrifice other's life below 1, for example with sacrificing Minion Life.
Taking Damage
Damage is the process by which a player or monster's life or energy shield is reduced.
Damage is always one of 5 damage types: physical, chaos, fire, cold or lightning.
Damage can be mitigated or prevented by various defences.
Damage can be:
Damage over time (DoT) refers to damage which happens gradually over a duration instead of all at once.
Hit damage is dealt instantaneously. Any damage that isn't damage over time is Hit damage.

title: Mana
text: Mana is a resource that can be used to pay for the costs of many skills. Mana cost is spent throughout the skill instead of on use; cancelling the skill or getting stunned will not consume mana. Most skills can be cancelled, with dodge roll forcibly cancelling most skills. The default attack does not cost mana. Mana naturally regenerates over time at a low rate. Using a skill with insufficient mana causes a blue visual effect near the character and plays a sound effect.

title: Mana
text:
Mana starts at 34 for level 1 characters, before factoring additional mana from intelligence.
Characters gain +4 maximum Mana per Player Level, +2 maximum Mana per intelligence.
All characters have a default mana regeneration rate of 4% of maximum mana that does not increase with levels.

text: The player is considered to be on full mana if they are at 100% of maximum mana or higher through overflow, unless mana is being reserved.

title: Meta
text: Meta skills are those that allow you to socket other active skills as support gems. Meta gems are often used to trigger active skills or change its functionality (for example, summoning a totem that attacks with a socketed skill).

title: Meta
text: Most trigger meta gems generate and use Energy, a counter that balances the frequency of triggering the skill based on its use time. The rate that Energy is obtained may be influenced by enemy Power, a stat dependent on the enemy's rarity.

title: Mind Over Matter
text: Mind Over Matter is a keystone passive skill that causes the character's mana to absorb all of the damage dealt to life, but halves mana recovery.

title: Mind Over Matter
text:
All damage that would be inflicted on the character's life is deducted from mana instead. If the character has insufficient mana, then the remainder of the damage will be taken from life.
As Mind Over Matter does not actually reduce total incoming damage or increase the player's actual life total, it does not affect the threshold or effectiveness of stun and ailments applied to players.
When combined with Chaos Inoculation, both energy shield and mana must be depleted before any damage affects life.
If both Chaos Inoculation and Eldritch Battery are taken, the player must fully deplete the enhanced mana pool before taking any damage to life. The player will still be technically immune to Bleeding as they will take all damage to mana first before life.
In the Trial of the Sekhemas, Mind over Matter will cause the player's maximum mana to be added to their total Honour, in addition to life and energy shield.

title: Minion
text: Minions are allies summoned or raised by the player's skills, effects, or buffs. Minions do not benefit from modifiers to stats that affect the player character's offences or defences; only modifiers that specify or affect minions or allies will apply.

title: Minion
text:
Permanent minions are minions that require typically require reservation of spirit.
The types and number of permanent minions to be summoned are selected in the skill menu, after which they are summoned automatically as long as the requirements and reservation amounts are met. They cannot be summoned manually using the skill. Permanent minions will revive themselves automatically if no other allied reviving minions have died within 7.5 seconds. Whenever a reviving minion dies during this period, the timer increases (capped at total 7.5 seconds), but each subsequent death will increase the timer by less each time. The value of the added timer is scaled as revival time per minion death. So the second death is +3,75s; the third +2,5s; fourth +1,875s etc.
"Reforming" is a more stricter condition of reviving that only occurs when a permanent minion revives after the revival timer ends. Minions revived in other ways do not count as reformed.
Permanent minions are capped at 255; exceeding this number will loop back to 0. This cap is per minion type.

It is used to determine the player's walk/run speed, as well as the speed of a dodge roll. The base movement speed modifier of a player is treated as 0% in the Miscellaneous section of the Character screen, which can be interpreted as 100% of base movement speed.

title: Oracle
text: The Oracle uses the power of Foresight to outmatch his foes and unlock new abilities. With Fateful Vision, the Oracle can see his future self using a random skill, which gets empowered if he does the same. With Converging Paths, he can bring a future vision of an enemy about to become immobilised into the present to harm it while it's vulnerable. The Oracle can manipulate the odds in his favor with The Lesser Harm to make enemy damage and critical hit chance unlucky, and Forced Outcome to always guarantee his hits become critical hits, at the cost of potential damage. The Unseen Path allows the Oracle to take passives on the passive skill tree no other classes have access to, and Entwined Realities to allocate unconnected passives near keystones. Additionally, Unnamed Heartwood grants additional totem limit and delays their death, and Harmony Within grants an alternative way to use mana as a life pool.

title: Pathfinder
text: The Pathfinder is a survival specialist with a focus in flasks, mobility, and flexibility with the passive skill tree.  Enduring Elixirs allows her life flasks to continue recovering her life even after recovering to full, and she can learn one of five Concoction skills to turn her mana flask into a source of damage. Relentless Pursuit and Running Assault keeps her mobile by mitigating effects that can reduce her movement speed or stop her entirely. The Pathfinder can gain a second starting point on the passive skill tree with Path Seeker and gain additional choices of stat bonuses on the travel nodes from Traveller's Wisdom. Other passives include Overwhelming Toxicity to double the number of poison stacks, and Sustainable Practices to gain elemental damage reduction from evasion.

title: Penetration
text:
Penetration causes the specified amount to be subtracted from the target's corresponding resistance when determining the damage they take from a hit, to a minimum of 0% resistance by default.
Penetration is calculated after accounting for other modifiers that raise or lower the target's resistances and their maximum capped resistances.

title: Physical
text:
Physical damage is one of the five damage types. Most martial weapons deal physical damage. Physical damage from hits is mitigated by armour and other sources of physical damage reduction.
Physical damage over time is usually inflicted by bleeding or Corrupted Blood. Armour has no effect on damage over time.

title: Physical
text:
Physical is the only damage type without a resistance; instead, it has a stat called physical damage reduction, to which armour contributes. Overwhelm directly ignores physical damage reduction similar to penetration, but cannot go below zero. Armour break, however, can go below zero.
Physical damage is the default damage type for attacks, and almost all martial weapons have base physical damage. Local physical damage modifiers and quality affect the physical damage of weapons.
Physical damage is 50% more likely to stun an enemy and causes 50% more Heavy Stun buildup than other damage types.

title: Poison
text:
Poison deals 20% of a hit's combined physical and chaos damage dealt (before mitigation and damage taken modifiers) as chaos damage over time over 2 seconds. This percentage is affected multiplicatively by ailment effect/magnitude. Ailment damage cannot be scaled directly; however, it can be indirectly scaled by modifying the hit damage.
Poison can stack and has a default stack limit of 1; this can be increased through various stats or modifiers. Each instance of poison has an independent duration and only the highest damage instance(s) of poisons up to your stack limit will deal damage.
The character's poison stack limit also applies to external poison sources such as Poison Clouds.
Poison chance depends on an explicit chance to poison.
The damage over time from poison bypasses energy shield and damages life directly.

title: Power charge
text:
Power charges are a resource that players can gain and generate in various ways. Charges do not inherently grant bonuses to the character or monsters; they are used to empower skills by being consumed by them.
Power charges, like other charges, have a default duration of 15 seconds and a maximum of 3.

text:
Different sources that grant a chance for spells to fire additional projectiles calculate those chances independently.

Player projectile skills will always fire at least 1 projectile, even if projectile count should be reduced to 0.

title: Projectile
text:
When using a skill that fires multiple projectiles, they can be fired in patterns:
Cone: The default pattern for a skill that only has additional projectiles without a specific pattern.
The cone angle narrows as the aiming distance increases to a minimum angle.
Spiral: will fire projectiles sequentially from right to left in a circle around the user at fixed angles. Additional projectiles typically increase the rotation of the spiral.
Circle: will fire projectiles simultaneously around the user at equidistant angles based on the number of projectiles.

title: Projectile
text:
When a projectile collides with an enemy or another entity, it either ends or continues based on one of the projectile behaviors described below.
If multiple projectiles are fired simultaneously, only one of them can collide with the same target, unless otherwise stated (e.g. Freezing Shards) or if the skills states the projectiles can Merge (e.g. Fragmentation Rounds).
This does not apply to projectiles fired in sequence, allowing them to hit the same target.

title: Projectile
text:
Projectile behaviours follow a specific order:
Cannot Collide: Prevents projectiles from hitting enemies while in flight and prevents other behavours. Projectiles can still hit the enemy if they have an area of effect component that either do not require collision or occurs when hitting the ground or terrain (e.g. walls).
Split: Causes projectiles to each fire towards multiple targets within 6 metres after hitting an initial target.
Split projectiles that have no valid targets will fire in random directions.
Pierce: Allows projectiles to continue their trajectory after hitting an entity on their path.
Piercing can occur up to N times. Each pierce has an independent chance to occur.
Fork: Causes projectiles to create two copies upon hitting a target.
These copies are fired at a fixed angle from the target hit by the original projectile.
Chain: Redirects a single projectile to the nearest target within chain range that has not been hit by other projectiles from the same group.
Chaining can occur up to N times per projectile.

Additional projectiles created by splits or forks are considered continuations of the original projectile, sharing the maximum travel distance and are unable to hit a previously hit target unless otherwise stated.
The following are miscellaneous projectile behaviours:
Bounce: Allows projectiles to bounce from walls or terrain in a random direction. Not to be confused with Chain, which requires a target within chain range. However, certain skills may gain convert additional chains into additional bounces.

title: Projectile
text: AOE: Some skills throw projectiles that trigger their effects on an area of effect when they are destroyed, reach end of flight, and/or collide with entities. Projectiles that only deal an area effect when the projectile is destroyed will not proc the AOE when the projectile pierces, chains, or forks.

title: Projectile
text:
Whenever a projectile collides, it will attempt each of its remaining behaviors
Projectile behaviors occur in the following order, if applicable:
Split
Pierce
Fork
Chain
For example:
A projectile first hits a target and splits towards a second target.
The projectile pierces the next N targets.
If a projectile can pierce indefinitely, further behaviors will never activate.
Terrain cannot be pierced.
The next target on its path that does not get pierced causes the projectile to fork into two projectiles.
The forked projectiles then chain N times until no valid targets remain or chaining is exhausted.
Different behaviors cannot occur simultaneously; the priority order determines how they occur.

title: Receiving damage
text: Receiving damage involves several steps to determine whether the damage hits, how much damage is dealt by the attacker, how much of that damage is prevented by the defender's mitigation, and what resources (e.g. life, energy shield) are ultimately lost as a result.

title: Receiving damage
text:
The list below displays the order of operations when an attacker attempts to damage a defender:
Avoiding the hit:
Manually avoiding hits via movement
Damage avoidance frames from dodge roll
Avoidance of projectiles
Evasion against (vs accuracy of) attacks or monster skills
These are the only defensive mechanics that prevent a hit from occurring, including preventing all on-hit effects. Other forms of mitigation cannot prevent a hit, even if they reduce damage taken to 0.

Rolling for damage:

title: Receiving damage
text:
After the previous multipliers are applied to the hit's minimum and maximum damage range, it now randomly chooses a number within this range. If the attacker's damage is lucky, or damage against the defender is unlucky, damage rolls twice and ignores the lower value. Similarly, if the attacker's damage is unlucky, damage rolls twice and ignores the higher value. This does not affect rolls for other mechanics (e.g. crit, ailments, block, suppression).
Doubling/tripling damage:
Modifiers that double or triple damage apply after other offensive damage modifiers.
Cannot take damage:
Damage is removed by modifiers that make the defender unable to take damage, such as Cannot take Reflected Physical/Elemental Damage or Proximal Tangibility. This is not conversion, though it is mechanically similar. Damage types can only be shifted once and all damage shift effects apply simultaneously. Additionally, damage shift is not proportional when exceeding 100% of a base damage type; for example, if a player has 120% physical to fire damage shift, they will take more base fire damage than they would have originally taken as physical.
Similar to conversion with damage modifiers, shifted damage is only affected by mitigation for its final damage type. For example, if physical damage is taken as fire, the shifted fire damage will not be affected by physical damage reduction.
Damage mitigation:
Cannot take X damage applies again here, preventing damage that wasn't already removed before the damage taken as step. This step does count as preventing damage.

text:
Resistance mitigates elemental and chaos damage. Effects such as exposure or area penalties apply here. The attacker's penetration applies afterward to the final resistance value, though it cannot penetrate below 0% resistance. If the resistance is at 0% or negative, penetration has no effect.
Modifying damage taken:
After damage mitigation has calculated base damage taken, modifiers to damage taken are applied. Flat modifiers are applied first, then the sum of all increases/reductions, and lastly all more or less multipliers independently:
Deflection
Deflection reduces damage after damage taken modifiers, but still applies for ailments.
Stun, Pin and ailment thresholds:
Stun, Pin and elemental ailment chance/buildup is rolled based on damage at this point.
Blocking the damage:

Damage is taken from energy shield before life, unless damage can bypass energy shield.

Energy shield recharge is interrupted when energy shield or the resource it is protecting is lost due to damage, unless recharge explicitly cannot be interrupted (e.g. Energy Barrier).
If Eternal Youth is allocated, only directly losing life due to damage will interrupt life recharge. Life loss over time (e.g. from Grasping Wounds) does not interrupt life recharge. Spending or sacrificing life does not interrupt recharge.

title: Receiving damage
text:
Damage over time generally follows the same principles; however, damage over time does not hit, bypassing many hit-based defensive mechanics such as evasion, armour, block, etc. Damage over time occurs at the start of each server frame, before potential hit damage, though after over-time recovery.
While damaging ailments are applied by hits, their damage is calculated as a percentage of the hit's damage before mitigations. This percentage is modified by ailment magnitude; no other damage multipliers will apply to prevent "double-dipping". Mitigation applies to damage over time after this independently of hit damage. This prevents debuffs like ignite from scaling twice with stats like #% increased Fire damage, but also prevents it from being mitigated twice by Fire Resistance.

title: Recoup
text: Recoup is a stat that causes your character to recover damage taken (or prevented) from a hit as life, mana, or energy shield over a duration.

title: Recoup
text:
In Path of Exile 2, Recoup occurs over 8 seconds by default. Recoup is normally calculated based on the damage taken after resistance from hits. Some passive nodes will instead activate recoup based on damage prevented. Each instance of recoup works independently. Damage over time effects will not activate recoup. Recoup continues even if the resource is full.
The duration of recoup can be modified by certain passive nodes. Reducing the duration of recoup will not reduce the amount recovered, instead recovering the same amount over a shorter time.

title: Regeneration
text: Regeneration is a form of recovery method for some resources, most commonly life and mana. Regeneration gives the appropriate resource a constant recovery per second rate.

text: Stats worded as "when you collect a Remnant" do not give you the benefits of these stats when an Ally shares the effects of a Remnant with you.

title: Resistance
text:
Resistance is a form of damage reduction that reduces damage of a particular type by a percentage. Players and enemies all have a resistance stat to each of Fire, Cold, Lightning and Chaos damage, and these are raised or lowered independently. Increases to "Elemental Resistance" are applied to fire, cold and lightning but not chaos.
Resistance has a default value of 0, where it does not affect the damage taken. Maximum resistances are soft capped at 75% by default but can be increased to a hard cap of 90%. Resistance can go into the negatives, which increases damage taken.
Characters receive a -10% penalty to elemental resistance approximately around the end of each act up until Act 4. During the Interludes, elemental resistance penalties are applied by area level. By endgame, the cumulative penalty is -60% to all elemental resistances.
Honour Resistance is a stat used exclusively in Trial of the Sekhemas, and is calculated the same way.

text: Having Penetration in a damage type reduces the effective resistance of enemies you damage with that type, thus increasing the damage they take. It stacks with exposure and curse debuffs, but is applied last and is only effective against positive resistances; it has no effect once the effective resistance is 0 or negative. title: Ritualist
text: The Ritualist has adopted the darker arts of the Azmeri. With Corrupted Lifeforce, she afflicts enemies with Blood Boils that spread Corrupted Blood on the victim's death and deals more damage against afflicted targets. With Wildwood Persistance, she can rapidly heal herself back from the brink. She can perform Ritual Sacrifice on slain monsters to steal their modifiers, or offer her own blood to gain a random monster modifier. The Ritualist can also specialize in items, enhancing her charms with Intricate Sigils and Mind Phylacteries, enhancing the effects of jewelry with Mystic Attunement, and even gain a third ring slot with Unfurled Finger.

title: Runic Ward
text: Runic Ward (or Ward) is a resource granted by items related to Expedition. If the user's life is reduced below 1, damage will be taken from Runic Ward to attempt to prevent the user's death. Runic Ward is also used as a cost for Kalguuran skills.

title: Runic Ward
text:
Mechanically, Runic Ward can be thought of as energy shield in reverse; all damage will be taken from life before runic ward. If an instance of damage were to exceed the user's life and runic ward pool, they will still die.
Runic Ward has a base regeneration rate of 5% per second.
Monsters with any amount of Runic Ward are immune to Culling Strike.

title: Shaman
text: The Shaman unleashes the force of nature upon his foes. Druidic Champion causes his rage to benefit spellcasting power, and Furious Wellspring lets him passively regenerate rage at the cost of adding a rage cost to his skills. The Shaman gains access to passives that grant Adaptation to help defend him against elemental damage that was previously dealt to him. With Turning of the Season, the Shaman gains improved elemental damage and exposure effect, and Bringer of the Apocalypse lets the Shaman unleash an elemental Apocalypse onto the battlefield after dealing enough elemental damage. Sacred Flow grants additional spirit for each empty charm slot, and Wisdom of the Maji unlocks hidden powers within in Runes and Idols.

title: Shock
text:
Shock grants a debuff of 20% increased Damage taken. This is additive with other damage taken modifiers.
Shock does not stack; each instance of shock has an independent duration and only the highest effect shock will apply (though there are things that change this rule, such as Stormweaver's ascendancy node Strike Twice).
The chance to apply shock depends on the damage taken by the enemy after mitigation relative to the enemy's ailment threshold. It is a base of 25% chance to apply per 100% of ailment threshold the hit deals. Unlike PoE1, critical hits do not inherently always apply ailments, but they do indirectly affect the chance to apply ailments due to critical damage bonus affecting the damage dealt.
Default shock if otherwise unspecified is 20%. This value can be increased through modifiers to effect/magnitude of shock; shock is capped at a maximum of 100%.
Base shock duration is 8 seconds on non-characters and 4 seconds on characters.

title: Skill speed
text:
More specific variants of skill speed only applicable to specific types of skills stack additively with skill speed. Examples include:
Attack speed for attacks and crossbow reload speed
Cast speed for spells
Throw speed for traps
Totem placement speed for totems
Warcry speed for warcries
Reload speed for crossbows (also directly scaled by local attack speed)

The final use time of a skill can be determined by converting a skill's use time into uses per second, then applying modifiers to skill speed or variants thereof.

text: Non-channelling actions can be performed once per server frame, which is 33 milliseconds. This means you can perform up to 30.3 actions per second. title: Smith of Kitava
text: The Smith of Kitava has honed his blacksmithing with the power of the god Kitava. He can make his weapon more lethal by forging it into an ally with Manifest Weapon, prepping it with Temper Weapon to give it explosive hits, or make it unleash fire spells on hit with Heat of the Forge. The Smith of Kitava can scale elemental resistances effectively thanks to Coal Stoker and Forged in Flame, by having fire resistance scale his cold and lightning resistances as well. With Smith's Masterwork, he can spend passive points to add powerful mods of his choosing to a Normal body armour.

The Sorceress is a Maraketh from the Vastiri Deserts. She was banished from her akhara for unspecified reasons; on her accord, she had left the Maraketh before taking an oath that would have bound her to them.
The Sorceress was also to be a tale-woman before her banishment.

title: Spell
text: Spells are skills that are cast or triggered by the user which can deal damage to an enemy or apply positive or negative effects to the caster, allies, or enemies. It is one of the two major categories for skills, the other being attacks. Unlike attacks, spells are not affected by accuracy or evasion.

title: Spirit
text: Spirit is a resource that can be reserved to activate persistent buffs, summon permanent minions, and enable trigger meta gems. Characters have no spirit by default, though they can gain up to 100 permanent Spirit through quest rewards during the campaign. Otherwise, spirit is primarily granted by equipment and ascendancy passives.

title: Stun
text: A Stun is an on-hit effect that causes the affected target to have their actions interrupted and be unable to act for a short period of time. Stun is separated into two types: Light Stun, which has a chance to briefly interrupt targets based on the damage, and Heavy Stun, which lasts longer and is accumulated on the target.

title: Stun
text:
Hits have a chance to stun to apply a Light Stun based on their damage compared to the target's maximum life. The chance to apply Light Stun scales up to 100% chance for hits that deal 100% of the target's maximum life. Any chance below 15% is discarded. Blocked hits still have a chance to Light Stun. Light Stun lasts 0.53 seconds.
Players have 50% more Light Stun Threshold per time they were Light Stunned in the past 4 seconds.

title: Stun
text:
All non-Cold damage from a hit adds Heavy Stun buildup to the hit's target, based on the damage of the hit, including blocked hits. Enemy's Heavy Stun buildup can be seen as a bar under their Life bar. Heavy Stun buildup decreases over time if the target has not had any Heavy Stun buildup applied to them for a certain period of time, or rapidly after a Heavy Stun animation finishes.
Cold damage cannot build up Heavy Stun (it applies Chill and build up Freeze instead).
Physical damage, and player (but not monster) Melee Damage, each cause 50% more Heavy Stun buildup. For players, these bonuses are multiplicative with each other (for a combined 125% more Heavy Stun buildup).

title: Stun
text:
When a target's Heavy Stun threshold is reached (when a target's Stun buildup is filled), it goes into a longer stun animation; the duration of the heavy stun depends on the specific monster. The Duration of an inflicted Stun is based on the Damage dealt by the Hit relative to the target's Stun Threshold, with higher Damage Hits resulting in longer Stuns. Heavy Stunned targets are considered to be Immobilised. Heavy Stun buildup cannot occur while the target is Heavy Stunned or while Heavy Stun buildup empties after a Heavy Stun animation finishes. After inflicting a Heavy Stun, it becomes harder to apply more Heavy Stun to the target.
Player minions cannot be Heavy Stunned unless otherwise specified.

title: Stun
text:
Players cannot be directly Heavy Stunned unless otherwise specified.
Player Heavy Stun can accumulate while active blocking (Raise Shield and Parry) or riding a mount (Rhoa Mount). They can also receive a Heavy Stun if they receive a hit while sprinting. Player Heavy Stun lasts 3 seconds. Players cannot evade or block while Heavy Stunned.

title: Stun
text:
Physical damage and melee hits are more effective at applying stun.
For players, both physical damage and melee hits have 50% more chance to apply Light Stun and 50% more Heavy Stun buildup. These bonuses are multiplicative, meaning a physical melee hit is 125% more effective at stunning than damage types of neither.
For monsters, melee attacks have 33% more Light Stun chance and Heavy Stun buildup, and physical damage has 100% more. These bonuses are also multiplicative, meaning monster melee physical hits have 166% more chance to stun than hits of neither.

title: Stun
text:
Stun threshold modifies the amount of stun buildup needed to inflict a stun. Increasing stun threshold reduces the chance of receiving a light stun and the amount of heavy stun accumulated, and vice versa.
Players have a base Stun Threshold value equal to their maximum life.

title: Stun
text: Primed for Stun is active on targets that have a certain percentage of Heavy Stun built up. Normal enemies are Primed for Stun when they have at least 40% Heavy Stun buildup. Magic enemies are instead Primed at 50% buildup, Rare at 60%, and Unique at 70%.

title: Tactician
text: The Tactician is a class specializing in defenses and empowering allies. He has access to lower reservation costs and the ability to give bonus damage to allies using his weapon or placing down Banners without limit. The Tactician can specialize in crowd control, improving his ability to immobilise enemies and turn Pin into a full disable. He also lends well to Armour/Evasion hybrid builds and enhancing the survivability they provide. He can also specialize in totems or call down Supporting Fire to rain down a volley of arrows on his foes.

title: Titan
text: The Titan is a class that possesses tremendous vitality and might. He can deliver powerful slams that can be ancestrally boosted and leave extra aftershocks, and improve his Heavy Stuns by making them easier to apply and dealing more damage to stunned enemies. The Titan can also be built to be very resilient with access to more life and armour. He can also gain extra inventory space from Colossal Capacity, which unlocks the ability to improve the power of his small passive skills from Hulking Form.

title: Warbringer
text: The Warbringer draws strength from his Karui and Ezomyte ancestry. The class improves his ability to block attacks and Break Armour, making them more vulnerable to physical damage and other damage types. He has the ability to enhance his totems to summon Ancestral Spirits and redirect incoming damage towards it, encase himself with jade to absorb damage from hits, and unleash warcries that explode corpses while ignoring their cooldowns.

title: Witchhunter
text: The Witchhunter has access to passives that grant general offensive bonuses, as well as specialized bonuses towards certain types of enemies. The Witchhunter is a potent boss killer, with access to Culling Strike and Decimating Strike to remove a chunk of their life, and the ability to reduce the enemy's Concentration and make them more vulnerable to damage and use their special abilities less frequently as you continue to hurt them. Sorcery Ward gives him an elemental barrier in exchange for armour and evasion, Zealous Inquisition adds pack-clearing power with infrequent but powerful on-kill explosions, and Weapon Master allows for more variety between weapon set passive trees.

title: Planner heuristics: balancing defences and damage
text:
# Planner heuristics: balancing defences and damage
These notes are the planner's own heuristics, not game data. They summarise common build-planning practice and point to the wiki pages (also in this knowledge base) for the exact mechanics. When a wiki chunk contradicts a heuristic here, the wiki wins.

title: Planner heuristics: balancing defences and damage
text:
A character dies from the single weakest defensive layer, not from the average. Damage still matters: killing faster removes threats before they act, and a build that cannot kill its content takes more hits over a longer fight. The planner therefore treats survivability and damage as a pair: fix hard defensive holes first, then spend on whichever side gives the larger measured gain per currency for the guide's stage.
Order of priority used by the planner:
1. Hard problems PoB reports: unmet attribute requirements (the item or gem stops working), over-reserved Spirit (buffs or minions switch off), uncapped elemental resistances.
2. The weakest damage type in PoB's "maximum hit taken" numbers (Physical, Fire, Cold, Lightning, Chaos). If one of them is far below the others, raising it is usually the best survivability purchase.
3. The guide's stated thresholds and slot priorities for the current stage.
4. Damage upgrades, measured as CombinedDPS gain per exalted orb.

title: Planner heuristics: balancing defences and damage
text:
Elemental resistances cap at 75% by default, and the campaign applies cumulative penalties to elemental resistance (see the wiki Resistance page for the current amounts). Each point near the cap removes a larger share of the remaining damage, so the last few percent to the cap are worth more than they look. Uncapped elemental resistance is the most common avoidable cause of deaths, so the planner fixes it before buying damage.
Chaos resistance usually starts at 0% and is not covered by "all elemental resistances" modifiers. It deserves more weight for energy-shield characters, because chaos damage removes twice as much energy shield (wiki: Energy Shield, Chaos). Characters with Chaos Inoculation are immune to chaos damage, so chaos resistance is irrelevant for them.

title: Planner heuristics: balancing defences and damage
text:
Armour, Evasion and Energy Shield are tied to Strength, Dexterity and Intelligence respectively, and armour pieces that grant a defence carry that attribute's requirement (wiki: Defences). A class's natural attribute therefore suggests its natural defence: Intelligence classes such as the Sorceress and Witch usually stack energy shield; Strength classes armour; Dexterity classes evasion; hybrids mix two.
- Armour reduces physical damage from hits and works best against many small hits; it does little against very large hits and nothing against damage over time (wiki: Armour).
- Evasion avoids hits entirely based on evasion rating versus enemy accuracy, and can downgrade critical hits (wiki: Evasion). Deflection supplements evasion builds and also works against boss attacks that evasion cannot stop (wiki: Deflection).
- Energy Shield is an extra pool on top of life that recharges when not damaged for a short time. Bleeding and poison bypass it to hit life directly, and chaos damage removes it twice as fast (wiki: Energy Shield).

title: Planner heuristics: balancing defences and damage
text:
Spending on a stat the build cannot use is wasted currency. Typical cases:
- Spell builds gain nothing from attack speed, accuracy or added attack damage; attack builds gain nothing from spell damage or cast speed.
- Pure energy-shield builds with Chaos Inoculation or low-life setups gain little from maximum life; small amounts of armour or evasion on such characters add little compared with more energy shield.
- Minion stats matter only when minions deal the damage or carry the defence; a self-cast build with a utility minion should ignore most of them.
- Item rarity and light radius do not improve the build's combat numbers.
- Overcapped resistance beyond the cap only helps against curses and exposure that lower it; a small buffer is useful, a large one is wasted.

title: Planner heuristics: balancing defences and damage
text:
- TotalEHP summarises how much damage the character can take; compare it before and after each change rather than in isolation.
- The per-type maximum hit taken shows the largest single hit of each type the character survives; the lowest one is the weakest link.
- CombinedDPS is the main damage figure; check that the guide's main skill is the one PoB is measuring.
- Requirement checks (Str, Dex, Int versus their requirements) and SpiritUnreserved below zero are hard failures, not trade-offs.

title: Planner heuristics: balancing defences and damage
text: Damage scales multiplicatively across categories: base damage (gem level, added damage, weapon), increased modifiers (which add together), more multipliers, critical hit chance and critical damage bonus, speed, and enemy resistance reduction (penetration, exposure, curses). Adding to a category the build has little of yields more than stacking one that is already large; the engine measures this directly, so the planner compares candidates by measured CombinedDPS gain (wiki: Damage, Critical hit, Penetration, Exposure).
